why: People step on the scale more than once a day. The one that counts is the last by the clock, and here the earlier reading is written second — so an implementation that takes whichever came last in the array reports 82 instead of 80.

checks.ordering: The 21:00 weigh-in wins over the 07:00 one regardless of the order they appear in the array.
checks.whyThisCaseExists: Rust fixed this in an early round; the Python reader kept resolving by array position for six rounds afterwards, and no corpus case had two measurements on one day, so nothing noticed. The four implementations only cross-check each other on the cases the corpus actually contains.
